# Action log (/docs/components/action-log)

An action log is a streaming list of what the agent does: each read, search, edit or command
lands as a row, running with a spinner, then done with a check and the time it took. A row with
output opens to show it, like a diff or test run. The header shows a spinner while the run is live
and a green dot once it finishes.

<Preview>
  <ActionLogExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + action-log.css -->
<div class="alg panel">
  <div class="alg-h">
    <span class="alg-t">Agent activity</span>
    <span class="alg-st"><span class="spin"></span><span class="alg-sum">Running</span></span>
  </div>
  <ol class="alg-list"></ol>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ActionLog } from './action-log/ActionLog';

<ActionLog
  title="Agent activity"
  running
  actions={[
    { icon: 'file-text', title: <>Read <code>Pricing.tsx</code></>, detail: 'src/pages, 212 lines', state: 'done', time: '0.4s' },
    { icon: 'term', title: <>Ran <code>npm test</code></>, detail: '24 tests passed', state: 'running' },
  ]}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ActionLogComponent] -->
<dm-action-log
  title="Agent activity"
  [running]="true"
  [actions]="actions"
></dm-action-log>

// actions: Action[] = [
//   { icon: 'file-text', title: 'Read <code>Pricing.tsx</code>', detail: 'src/pages, 212 lines', state: 'done', time: '0.4s' },
//   { icon: 'term', title: 'Ran <code>npm test</code>', detail: '24 tests passed', state: 'running' },
// ];
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/action_log.dart';

ActionLog(
  running: true,
  actions: const [
    Action(icon: Icons.description_outlined, title: 'Read Pricing.tsx', detail: 'src/pages, 212 lines', state: ActionState.done, time: '0.4s'),
    Action(icon: Icons.terminal, title: 'Ran npm test', detail: '24 tests passed', state: ActionState.running),
  ],
)
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | `Action[]` | The tool calls, newest at the end. Each has an `icon`, a `title`, an optional `detail`, a `state` of running or done, an optional `time`, and optional `output`. |
| `title` | `string` | The header text. Defaults to "Agent activity". |
| `running` | `boolean` | Shows a spinner in the header while true, and a green dot once false. |
| `status` | `string` | The words beside the header mark. Defaults to "Running step N", then "N steps, Xs". |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set false to give it a card of its own. |
| `onToggle` / `toggleRow` | `callback` | Fires when a row opens or closes. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the rows and the output panes are squared off with hairline edges; in Soft they are
rounded chips with soft fills. Added and removed lines in a row's output take the add and remove
colors from the tokens.


# Agent phases (/docs/components/agent-phases)

Agent phases show which phase the agent is in, in one line: its glyph, its name shimmering while the
phase lasts, and the seconds so far, with a track of six short segments under it that fills phase by
phase. When the agent needs you, is slow or fails, a line under the track says so with what to do;
once it is done the line reads how long it took and opens to the phases it ran through.

<Preview>
  <AgentPhasesExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + agent-phases.css -->
<div class="aph" data-p="read">
  <button class="aph-h" aria-expanded="false" aria-disabled="true">
    <span class="aph-g"></span><span class="aph-l shim">Reading 3 articles</span>
    <span class="aph-t num">7s</span><svg class="i xs aph-chev"><use href="#i-chev-d"/></svg>
  </button>
  <div class="aph-tr" aria-hidden="true"><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i></div>
  <div class="aph-x"></div>
  <div class="fold shut aph-fold"><div><ol class="aph-list"></ol></div></div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { AgentPhases } from './agent-phases/AgentPhases';

<AgentPhases phase="reading" label="Reading 3 articles" />
<AgentPhases phase="searching" error={{ text: 'The search timed out', onRetry: retry }} />
<AgentPhases phase="reading" slow={{ text: 'Still working…', onStop: stop }} />
<AgentPhases phase="waiting" ask={{ text: 'Offer Maya a refund of $48?', onApprove: approve }} />
<AgentPhases phase="done" took={{ thinking: 2, searching: 3, reading: 4 }} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [AgentPhasesComponent] -->
<dm-agent-phases phase="reading" label="Reading 3 articles"></dm-agent-phases>
<dm-agent-phases phase="searching" [error]="searchError"></dm-agent-phases>
<dm-agent-phases phase="reading" [slow]="slowNote"></dm-agent-phases>
<dm-agent-phases phase="waiting" [ask]="refundAsk"></dm-agent-phases>
<dm-agent-phases phase="done" [took]="took"></dm-agent-phases>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/agent_phases.dart';

const AgentPhases(phase: AgentPhase.reading, label: 'Reading 3 articles'),
AgentPhases(phase: AgentPhase.searching, error: AgentPhasesError(text: 'The search timed out', onRetry: retry)),
AgentPhases(phase: AgentPhase.reading, slow: AgentPhasesSlow(text: 'Still working…', onStop: stop)),
AgentPhases(phase: AgentPhase.waiting, ask: AgentPhasesAsk(text: 'Offer Maya a refund of \$48?', onApprove: approve)),
const AgentPhases(phase: AgentPhase.done, took: {AgentPhase.thinking: 2, AgentPhase.searching: 3, AgentPhase.reading: 4}),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `phase` | `thinking \| searching \| reading \| waiting \| writing \| done` | Which phase the agent is in. |
| `label` | `string` | What the line says. Defaults to the phase's name; once done, "Thought for 12s". |
| `seconds` | `number` | Seconds so far. Counts by itself while left out, and stops while waiting for you. |
| `error` | `object` | A step that failed: the line turns red and says so, with Retry. Has `text`, optional `detail`, and `onRetry`. |
| `slow` | `object` | Shown while the phase takes long, with Stop. Has `text` and an optional `onStop`. |
| `ask` | `object` | What the agent waits for in the waiting phase. Has `text`, optional `approveLabel`, `onApprove` and optional `onDecline`. |
| `took` | `Record<phase, number>` | Seconds each phase took, for the list a finished line opens to. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | Whether the finished line is open. Leave `open` out to let the header toggle it. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The glyph
and the current segment take the phase's colour — the accent while it works, amber while it waits,
red on an error and green when done. In Blueprint the segments are squared off and the shimmer rests
on a solid colour.


# Badge (/docs/components/badge)

A badge is a compact label. Its `tone` picks the color (neutral, the accent tint, the three
states, or one of eight tag colors). Two sizes, an optional dot or icon before the label, and an
optional remove button after it.

<Preview>
  <BadgeExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + badge.css -->
<span class="bdg" data-tone="success">Live</span>
<span class="bdg live" data-tone="success"><span class="bdg-dot"></span>Running</span>
<span class="bdg sm" data-tone="accent">Pro</span>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Badge } from './badge/Badge';

<Badge tone="success">Live</Badge>
<Badge tone="success" dot>Running</Badge>
<Badge tone="accent" size="sm">Pro</Badge>
<Badge tone="warning" onRemove={() => drop()}>Production</Badge>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [BadgeComponent] -->
<dm-badge tone="success">Live</dm-badge>
<dm-badge tone="success" [dot]="true" [live]="true">Running</dm-badge>
<dm-badge tone="accent" size="sm">Pro</dm-badge>
<dm-badge tone="warning" [removable]="true" (remove)="drop()">Production</dm-badge>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/badge.dart';

const Badge('Live', tone: BadgeTone.success),
const Badge('Running', tone: BadgeTone.success, dot: true),
const Badge('Pro', tone: BadgeTone.accent, size: BadgeSize.sm),
Badge('Production', tone: BadgeTone.warning, onRemove: drop),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `neutral \| accent \| success \| warning \| danger \| blue \| violet \| green \| orange \| red \| yellow \| pink \| teal` | Color as text on its own tint. Neutral by default. |
| `size` | `sm \| md` | `sm` is 20px tall, `md` is 24px (the default). |
| `dot` | `boolean` | A dot in the badge's color before the label. |
| `icon` | `IconName` | An icon before the label. |
| `onRemove` / `remove` | `callback` | Shows a remove button after the label. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the badge is squared off and set in small caps with a hairline in its own color; in Soft
it is a pill.


# Browser session (/docs/components/browser-session)

A browser session shows the agent browsing the web for you: a small browser frame with the page it
is on, the steps it takes under it, and Pause and Take over. When a step waits for you — a cookie
banner in the way, say — it shows why and a button to let the agent go on. Take over hands the page
to you: its frame turns the accent colour, its controls become usable, and the button reads Hand
back.

<Preview>
  <BrowserSessionExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + browser-session.css -->
<div class="bws panel">
  <div class="bws-h">
    <div class="bws-ht"><b>Pricing research</b><span class="muted bws-st"></span></div>
    <div class="bws-ctl">
      <button class="ib bws-pause" aria-label="Pause"><svg class="i s"><use href="#i-pause"/></svg></button>
      <button class="pill line sm bws-take" aria-pressed="false">Take over</button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="bws-win"><div class="bws-bar"></div><div class="bws-vp"></div></div>
  <ol class="bws-steps" aria-label="Steps"></ol>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { BrowserSession } from './browser-session/BrowserSession';

<BrowserSession
  title="Pricing research"
  url="northwind.app/pricing"
  steps={[
    { label: 'Click "Pricing"', state: 'done' },
    { label: 'Read the plans table', state: 'waiting', detail: 'A cookie banner covers the table' },
  ]}
  ask={{ label: 'Allow closing it', onAllow: allow }}
>
  <div className="dm-bws-pg">{/* the page, drawn as a wireframe */}</div>
</BrowserSession>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [BrowserSessionComponent] -->
<dm-browser-session
  title="Pricing research"
  url="northwind.app/pricing"
  [steps]="steps"
  [ask]="cookieAsk"
>
  <ng-template #page>
    <div class="dm-bws-pg"><!-- the page, drawn as a wireframe --></div>
  </ng-template>
</dm-browser-session>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/browser_session.dart';

BrowserSession(
  title: 'Pricing research',
  url: 'northwind.app/pricing',
  steps: const [
    BrowserStep(label: 'Click "Pricing"', state: BrowserStepState.done),
    BrowserStep(label: 'Read the plans table', state: BrowserStepState.waiting, detail: 'A cookie banner covers the table'),
  ],
  ask: BrowserAsk(label: 'Allow closing it', onAllow: allow),
  page: const PricingWireframe(),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | What the agent is browsing for, like "Pricing research". |
| `url` | `string` | The address bar: the page's address, or the search being typed. |
| `search` | `boolean` | Marks `url` as a search, with a magnifier instead of the padlock. |
| `steps` | `BrowserStep[]` | The steps the agent takes. Each has a `label`, a `state` of `queued`, `running`, `waiting` or `done`, and an optional `detail`. |
| `cursor` | `object` | The agent's own pointer, in pixels from the page's top left. Hidden while you have control. |
| `ask` | `object` | While a step waits: the button that lets the agent go on. Has a `label` and `onAllow`. |
| `paused` / `defaultPaused` | `boolean` | Pause holds the agent where it is. Leave `paused` out to let the button toggle it. |
| `inControl` / `defaultInControl` | `boolean` | Take over hands the page to you. Leave `inControl` out to let the button toggle it. |
| `seconds` | `number` | Seconds to show as m:ss. Leave it out to let the clock count while browsing. |
| `status` | `string` | The line under the title. Defaults to a status word, then the clock. |
| `summary` | `string` | Shown under the steps once every step is done. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The page
is drawn small, with real words where they matter and grey lines for the rest; a price the agent has
taken is marked in the accent fill. While you have control the frame turns the accent colour. In
Blueprint the frame and chips are squared off.


# Buttons (/docs/components/buttons)

A button is a pill in one of the variants — `primary` for the main action, `soft` and `line` for the
rest, `ghost` for the quietest — in three sizes. Return a promise from `onClick` and the button runs
itself: it shows the busy face until the promise settles, then the done face. `ButtonCopy` copies
text and flashes a check.

<Preview>
  <ButtonsExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + buttons.css -->
<button class="dm-pill dm-primary">Primary</button>
<button class="dm-pill dm-accent">Accent</button>
<button class="dm-pill dm-soft" aria-pressed="false">Preview</button>
<button class="dm-pill dm-line">Line</button>
<button class="dm-pill dm-ghost">Ghost</button>

<!-- sizes -->
<button class="dm-pill dm-accent dm-sm">Small</button>
<button class="dm-pill dm-accent dm-btx-lg">Large</button>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonCopy } from './buttons/Buttons';

<Button variant="primary">Primary</Button>
<Button variant="soft" size="sm">Small</Button>

// return a promise and the button runs busy -> done by itself
<Button variant="primary" busyLabel="Publishing" doneLabel="Published" onClick={publish}>
  Publish
</Button>
<Button variant="accent" success onClick={save}>Save</Button>

<ButtonCopy text="https://designme.dev" label="Copy link" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ButtonComponent, ButtonCopyComponent] -->
<dm-button variant="primary">Primary</dm-button>
<dm-button variant="soft" size="sm">Small</dm-button>

<dm-button variant="primary" busyLabel="Publishing" doneLabel="Published" (click)="publish()">
  Publish
</dm-button>
<dm-button variant="accent" [success]="true" (click)="save()">Save</dm-button>

<dm-button-copy text="https://designme.dev" label="Copy link" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/buttons.dart';

const Button('Primary', variant: ButtonVariant.primary),
const Button('Small', variant: ButtonVariant.soft, size: ButtonSize.sm),

Button('Publish', variant: ButtonVariant.primary, busyLabel: 'Publishing', doneLabel: 'Published', onClick: publish),
Button('Save', variant: ButtonVariant.accent, success: true, onClick: save),

ButtonCopy(text: 'https://designme.dev', label: 'Copy link'),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `primary \| accent \| soft \| line \| ghost \| ink` | The style. Left out, a plain pill. `ink` is the old name for `primary`. |
| `size` | `sm \| md \| lg` | The three sizes; `md` is the default. |
| `icon` | `IconName` | An icon before the label. |
| `onClick` | `(e) => void \| Promise<unknown>` | Return a promise and the button runs busy then done by itself. |
| `busy` / `done` | `boolean` | Drive the busy or done face yourself. Clicks are ignored while shown. |
| `busyLabel` / `doneLabel` | `ReactNode` | The labels on the busy and done faces. |
| `busyGlyph` | `spin \| think` | The busy glyph: a spinner, or the agent's turning dots. |
| `success` | `boolean` | The done face turns green. |
| `pressed` | `boolean` | For a toggle: whether it is on, as `aria-pressed`. |
| `tip` / `kbd` | `string` | A tooltip, with an optional shortcut after it. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
variants read against the theme's accent and surface tokens; in Soft the pills are rounder and
softer, and the busy and done faces blur across in either theme.


# Context meter (/docs/components/context-meter)

A context meter is a pill with a ring that shows how full the context window is. It opens a panel
with one bar split by kind, a legend whose rows list what is in each part, and a Compact button
that summarises older turns to free room. The ring turns orange past a warning share, and a message
line fades in with a warning or a result.

<Preview>
  <ContextMeterExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + context-meter.css -->
<div class="ctm" data-open="1">
  <button class="ctm-tg" aria-expanded="true"><span class="ctm-ring"><svg viewBox="0 0 20 20"><circle class="tr" cx="10" cy="10" r="7.5"/><circle class="fl" cx="10" cy="10" r="7.5" pathLength="100"/></svg></span><span><span class="ctm-pc num">0%</span> of context used</span></button>
  <div class="ctm-pop panel">
    <div class="ctm-ph"><span>In context</span><span class="num"><b class="ctm-tot">0k</b> of 200k tokens</span></div>
    <div class="ctm-bar"></div>
    <div class="ctm-leg"></div>
    <div class="ctm-f"><span class="ctm-hint">Summarises older turns</span><button class="pill ghost sm ctm-go">Compact</button></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ContextMeter } from './context-meter/ContextMeter';

<ContextMeter
  limit={200000}
  parts={[
    { key: 'files', label: 'Files', tokens: 56200, items: 'PricingCard.tsx 18.2k, tokens.css 6.1k' },
    { key: 'tools', label: 'Tool output', tokens: 41800 },
    { key: 'chat', label: 'Chat', tokens: 32100 },
  ]}
  onCompact={async () => summarise()}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ContextMeterComponent] -->
<dm-context-meter
  [limit]="200000"
  [parts]="parts"
  (compact)="summarise()"
></dm-context-meter>

// parts: ContextPart[] = [
//   { key: 'files', label: 'Files', tokens: 56200, items: 'PricingCard.tsx 18.2k, tokens.css 6.1k' },
//   { key: 'tools', label: 'Tool output', tokens: 41800 },
//   { key: 'chat', label: 'Chat', tokens: 32100 },
// ];
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/context_meter.dart';

ContextMeter(
  limit: 200000,
  parts: const [
    ContextPart(key: 'files', label: 'Files', tokens: 56200, items: 'PricingCard.tsx 18.2k, tokens.css 6.1k'),
    ContextPart(key: 'tools', label: 'Tool output', tokens: 41800),
    ContextPart(key: 'chat', label: 'Chat', tokens: 32100),
  ],
  onCompact: () async => summarise(),
)
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parts` | `ContextPart[]` | What fills the context. Each has a `key`, a `label`, its `tokens`, an optional `color`, and optional `items` shown on hover. |
| `limit` | `number` | The size of the context window, in tokens, like 200000. |
| `warnAt` | `number` | From this share of the limit (0 to 1) the ring turns orange. Defaults to 0.85. |
| `message` | `string` | A line under the legend. Crossfades when it changes. |
| `messageTone` | `warn \| ok` | warn shows it in orange with a warning sign, ok in green with a check. |
| `compacted` | `boolean` | Set once compacted: the button turns into Undo. |
| `hint` | `string` | The quiet line beside the button. Defaults to "Summarises older turns". |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the panel is open. Leave it out to let the pill toggle it. |
| `onCompact` / `compact` | `callback` | Called by Compact. Return a promise and the button spins until it settles. |
| `onUndo` / `undo` | `callback` | Called by Undo once compacted. |
| `onOpenChange` / `openChange` | `callback` | Fires when the panel opens or shuts. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the pill, the bar and the panel are squared off; in Soft they are rounded. The ring takes
the accent mark and the warning mark past the warning share, and the bar segments take the part
palette (blue, teal, violet, grey) from the tokens unless a part sets its own color.


# Progress (/docs/components/progress)

Progress shows a long run three ways at once: a ring for the whole run, a segment per step, and a
bar for how far the step in hand has got. The `state` colours it — grey while indeterminate or
paused, the accent while running, red with a Retry on error, green when complete — and the controls
follow (Pause, Resume, Run again). An optional `meter` underneath warns in words as it fills.

<Preview>
  <ProgressExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + progress.css -->
<div class="dm-prg dm-panel" data-s="run">
  <div class="dm-prg-h">
    <span class="dm-prg-ring"><span class="dm-prg-pc dm-num">42%</span></span>
    <div class="dm-prg-t">
      <b>Indexing the docs</b>
      <span class="dm-muted dm-prg-vt">Step 2 of 4, embedding</span>
    </div>
    <span class="dm-tag dm-prg-st dm-run">Running</span>
    <button class="dm-ib dm-prg-btn" aria-label="Pause">⏸</button>
  </div>
  <div class="dm-prg-seg"><i><b></b></i><i><b></b></i></div>
  <div class="dm-prg-lin"><i style="width: 42%"></i></div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Progress } from './progress/Progress';

const steps = [
  { label: 'Reading files', unit: 'Files', total: 2000 },
  { label: 'Embedding', unit: 'Chunks', total: 5400 },
  { label: 'Writing', unit: 'Shards', total: 16 },
];

<Progress
  title="Indexing the docs"
  state="running"
  steps={steps}
  step={1}
  stepProgress={0.4}
  meter={{ label: 'Credits this month', value: 8558, max: 10000, warnAt: 0.75, note: 'Resets Dec 1' }}
  onPause={pause}
  onResume={resume}
  onRetry={retry}
  onRestart={restart}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ProgressComponent] -->
<dm-progress
  title="Indexing the docs"
  state="running"
  [steps]="steps"
  [step]="1"
  [stepProgress]="0.4"
  [meter]="meter"
  (pause)="onPause()"
  (resume)="onResume()"
  (retry)="onRetry()"
  (restart)="onRestart()"
></dm-progress>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/progress.dart';

Progress(
  title: 'Indexing the docs',
  state: ProgressState.running,
  steps: const [
    ProgressStep(label: 'Reading files', unit: 'Files', total: 2000),
    ProgressStep(label: 'Embedding', unit: 'Chunks', total: 5400),
  ],
  step: 1,
  stepProgress: 0.4,
  meter: const ProgressMeter(
    label: 'Credits this month', value: 8558, max: 10000, warnAt: 0.75, note: 'Resets Dec 1',
  ),
  onPause: pause,
  onResume: resume,
  onRetry: retry,
  onRestart: restart,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The run's name, like "Indexing the docs". |
| `state` | `indeterminate \| running \| paused \| error \| complete` | Colours the run and picks the control shown. |
| `steps` | `ProgressStep[]` | The steps, each `{ label, unit, total }`. |
| `step` | `number` | The step in hand, from `0`. |
| `stepProgress` | `number` | How far the step in hand has got, `0` to `1`. |
| `valueText` | `string` | The line under the title. Defaults to "Step 3 of 5, …". |
| `error` | `string` | What failed, shown over the bar while `state` is `error`. |
| `onPause` / `onResume` / `onRetry` / `onRestart` | `callback` | The controls, wired to the matching state. |
| `meter` | `ProgressMeter` | A meter under the run, with thresholds that warn in words. |

A `ProgressMeter` is `{ label, value, max, unit?, warnAt?, dangerAt?, dangerLabel?, note? }`: it
reads "On track" until `value / max` crosses `warnAt` ("Running low") and then `dangerAt` (the
`dangerLabel`, or "Almost out").

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the ring, segments and bar are squared off with hairline tracks; in Soft they are rounded
with a softer fill. The state colours and the meter's warn and danger bands come from the theme, so
they read correctly on either background.


# Reasoning trail (/docs/components/reasoning-trail)

A reasoning trail is the structured record the agent leaves after it thinks: a plan it works
through, the notes it took, the sources it read, or the edits it made. Pick what it shows with
`view`. The header counts the seconds and shimmers while the run is live, folds the trail away, and
settles on "Reasoned for Ns" once it finishes.

<Preview>
  <ReasoningTrailExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + reasoning-trail.css -->
<div class="rtr panel">
  <button class="rtr-h" aria-expanded="true">
    <span class="think on rtr-mark"><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i></span>
    <span class="rtr-title shim">Reasoning</span>
    <span class="rtr-time num muted">0s</span>
    <svg class="i xs rtr-chev"><use href="#i-chev-d"/></svg>
  </button>
  <div class="fold rtr-fold"><div><div class="rtr-body"></div></div></div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ReasoningTrail } from './reasoning-trail/ReasoningTrail';

<ReasoningTrail
  running
  view="plan"
  plan={[
    { label: 'Open the onboarding file', detail: '4 frames', state: 'done' },
    { label: 'Compare with the design system', state: 'now' },
    { label: 'Draft fixes for review', state: 'next' },
  ]}
  sources={[{ label: 'Onboarding.fig', kind: 'figma', tip: '4 frames read' }]}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ReasoningTrailComponent] -->
<dm-reasoning-trail
  [running]="true"
  view="plan"
  [plan]="plan"
  [sources]="sources"
  (viewChange)="view = $event"
></dm-reasoning-trail>

// plan: PlanStep[] = [
//   { label: 'Open the onboarding file', detail: '4 frames', state: 'done' },
//   { label: 'Compare with the design system', state: 'now' },
//   { label: 'Draft fixes for review', state: 'next' },
// ];
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/reasoning_trail.dart';

ReasoningTrail(
  running: true,
  view: ReasoningTrailView.plan,
  plan: const [
    PlanStep(label: 'Open the onboarding file', detail: '4 frames', state: PlanStepState.done),
    PlanStep(label: 'Compare with the design system', state: PlanStepState.now),
    PlanStep(label: 'Draft fixes for review', state: PlanStepState.next),
  ],
  sources: const [Source(label: 'Onboarding.fig', kind: SourceKind.figma, tip: '4 frames read')],
)
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `running` | `boolean` | Shimmers the title and counts the seconds while true. |
| `seconds` | `number` | Seconds to show. Leave it out to let the trail count while it runs. |
| `title` | `string` | Header text. Defaults to "Reasoning" while running and "Reasoned for Ns" after. |
| `plan` | `PlanStep[]` | The plan. Each step has a `label`, an optional `detail`, and a `state` of done, now or next. |
| `notes` | `string[]` | The agent's notes, one per line. |
| `sources` | `Source[]` | The files and links it read. Each has a `label`, an optional `kind`, and an optional `tip`. |
| `edits` | `Edit[]` | The changed files. Each has a `file`, an optional `detail`, and `removed` and `added` lines. |
| `view` | `plan \| notes \| sources \| edits` | Which part to show. Leave it out to start on the first one there is. |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the trail is open. Leave it out to let the header toggle it. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set false to give it a card of its own. |
| `onViewChange` / `viewChange` | `callback` | Fires when the shown view changes. |
| `onOpenChange` / `openChange` | `callback` | Fires when the trail opens or folds. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the header, chips and edit blocks are squared off with hairline edges; in Soft they are
rounded. The timeline rail, the pulse on the current step, and the shimmer on the title all take
their colors from the tokens; added and removed lines use the add and remove colors.


# Run cost (/docs/components/run-cost)

A run cost shows the credits a run has used against its budget, as a number and a meter. A cap
marks where the agent pauses, drawn as a line across the bar; when the spend reaches it the status
turns amber and the run pauses. The breakdown under the bar shows the tokens and tool calls behind
the number, and the button starts, stops, resumes or raises the cap by status.

<Preview>
  <RunCostExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + run-cost.css -->
<div class="rc panel">
  <div class="rc-h"><span class="muted">Credits used</span><span class="rc-st tag"><span class="dot"></span><span class="rc-stt">Idle</span></span></div>
  <div class="rc-big"><span class="rc-n num">0</span><span class="muted"> / 2,000</span></div>
  <div class="rc-track"><div class="rc-fill"></div><div class="rc-cap" data-tip="The agent pauses here"></div></div>
  <div class="rc-f">
    <label class="rc-cap-t"><button class="toggle" role="switch" aria-checked="true"></button><span>Pause at 90%</span></label>
    <button class="pill primary sm rc-go">Start run</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { RunCost } from './run-cost/RunCost';

<RunCost
  used={1620}
  budget={2000}
  capAt={90}
  status="running"
  rows={[
    { label: 'Input tokens', value: 14200 },
    { label: 'Output tokens', value: 3600 },
    { label: 'Tool calls', value: 7 },
  ]}
  onAction={() => stop()}
  onCapChange={(on) => setCap(on)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [RunCostComponent] -->
<dm-run-cost
  [used]="1620"
  [budget]="2000"
  [capAt]="90"
  status="running"
  [rows]="rows"
  (action)="stop()"
  (capChange)="cap = $event"
></dm-run-cost>

// rows: RunCostRow[] = [
//   { label: 'Input tokens', value: 14200 },
//   { label: 'Output tokens', value: 3600 },
//   { label: 'Tool calls', value: 7 },
// ];
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart

RunCost(
  used: 1620,
  budget: 2000,
  capAt: 90,
  status: RunCostStatus.running,
  rows: const [
    RunCostRow('Input tokens', 14200),
    RunCostRow('Output tokens', 3600),
    RunCostRow('Tool calls', 7),
  ],
  onAction: stop,
  onCapChange: (on) => setCap(on),
)
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `used` | `number` | Credits used so far. |
| `budget` | `number` | The whole budget, like 2000. |
| `capAt` | `number` | Where the agent pauses, as a percentage of the budget. Defaults to 90. |
| `capOn` | `boolean` | Whether the cap is on. Leave it out to let the switch change it. |
| `status` | `idle \| running \| stopped \| paused \| spent` | running is blue, paused amber, spent red. |
| `statusLabel` | `string` | Words in the status tag. Defaults by status. |
| `rows` | `RunCostRow[]` | The breakdown under the bar; each row has a `label` and a `value`. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | Words on the button. Defaults by status. |
| `title` | `string` | Defaults to "Credits used". |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set false to give it a card of its own. |
| `onAction` / `action` | `callback` | Called by the button. |
| `onCapChange` / `capChange` | `callback` | Fires when the cap switch changes. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the bar, the tag and the toggle are squared off; in Soft they are rounded. The fill takes
the accent mark while running and the warning mark once paused at the cap, and the status tag tints
to match its state, all from the tokens.


# Run queue (/docs/components/run-queue)

A run queue shows a batch of agent jobs moving through three parts. The job running is raised on
its own card with its agent, its steps, a progress bar and the time left. The jobs up next wait
below, each with when it should start, and the jobs done sit under them with how long each took and
a green tick. A failed step turns its job red and offers a Retry; a Detailed / Compact switch folds
the running job's steps away; and once every job is done a summary takes the running job's place.

<Preview>
  <RunQueueExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + run-queue.css, then the component script -->
<div class="card bare" data-c="run-queue">
  <div class="stage-in">
    <div class="rq panel keep">
      <div class="rq-h">
        <div class="rq-ht"><b>Launch prep</b><span class="rq-st num">4 jobs queued</span></div>
        <div class="seg2" role="group" aria-label="Density">
          <button aria-pressed="true" data-v="full">Detailed</button>
          <button aria-pressed="false" data-v="compact">Compact</button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="rq-tot" aria-hidden="true"></div>
      <div class="rq-b"><!-- running / up next / done sections --></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { RunQueue } from './run-queue/RunQueue';

const jobs = [
  { id: 'email', title: 'Draft the launch email', agent: 'Copy agent', state: 'running', time: '4.2s',
    steps: [
      { label: 'Outline', state: 'done', meta: 'done' },
      { label: 'Draft', state: 'running' },
      { label: 'Proofread', state: 'queued' },
    ] },
  { id: 'post', title: 'Schedule the posts', agent: 'Social agent', state: 'queued', time: 'in ~4s' },
];

<RunQueue title="Launch prep" jobs={jobs} summary="12.8s in all" onRetry={(j, s) => retry(j, s)} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [RunQueueComponent] -->
jobs: RunJob[] = [
  { id: 'email', title: 'Draft the launch email', agent: 'Copy agent', state: 'running', time: '4.2s',
    steps: [
      { label: 'Outline', state: 'done', meta: 'done' },
      { label: 'Draft', state: 'running' },
      { label: 'Proofread', state: 'queued' },
    ] },
  { id: 'post', title: 'Schedule the posts', agent: 'Social agent', state: 'queued', time: 'in ~4s' },
];
```

```html
<dm-run-queue
  title="Launch prep"
  [jobs]="jobs"
  summary="12.8s in all"
  (retry)="onRetry($event)"
  (densityChange)="onDensity($event)"
></dm-run-queue>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/run_queue.dart';

RunQueue(
  title: 'Launch prep',
  summary: '12.8s in all',
  onRetry: (job, step) => retry(job, step),
  jobs: const [
    RunJob(id: 'email', title: 'Draft the launch email', agent: 'Copy agent', state: RunState.running, time: '4.2s', steps: [
      RunStep(label: 'Outline', state: RunState.done, meta: 'done'),
      RunStep(label: 'Draft', state: RunState.running),
      RunStep(label: 'Proofread', state: RunState.queued),
    ]),
    RunJob(id: 'post', title: 'Schedule the posts', agent: 'Social agent', state: RunState.queued, time: 'in ~4s'),
  ],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jobs` | `RunJob[]` | The jobs in the queue. Each has a title, an agent, an icon, a state, an optional progress, a time, a note, and its steps. |
| `title` | `string` | The queue's name over its status line. |
| `status` | `string` | Overrides the status line. Defaults to "1 of 4 done" or "All 4 done". |
| `summary` | `string` | The line under "All N jobs done" once every job is done, like "18.4s in all · 1 retry". |
| `density` | `detailed \| compact` | detailed lists the running job's steps, compact folds them away. Left out, the switch changes it. |
| `onDensityChange` / `densityChange` | `callback` | Fires when the Detailed / Compact switch changes. |
| `onRetry` / `retry` | `callback` | Called by a failed step's Retry button with the job's and the step's index. Without it, failed steps show no button. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread, with no card. False by default. |

A `RunJob` state is queued, running, failed, or done. A `RunStep` has a label, a state, and an
optional meta shown once the step is done. Progress defaults to the share of a job's steps that are
done.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the running job gets a hairline in the accent and the progress bars fill in steps. A
failed job turns red with a hatched fill; the step glyphs are a spinner while running, a tick when
done, and a cross on failure.


# Segmented Control (/docs/components/segmented-control)

A segmented control picks one of a few options. A white knob slides to the picked one. As `tabs`
(the default) it switches a panel; as a `radio` group it sets an option. The arrow keys move along
and pick, and Home and End jump to the ends. The `label` is required and names the group for screen
readers.

<Preview>
  <SegmentedControlExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + segmented-control.css -->
<div class="sgc-seg" role="tablist" aria-label="View">
  <span class="sgc-k" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <button role="tab" aria-selected="true" data-v="day">Day</button>
  <button role="tab" aria-selected="false" tabindex="-1" data-v="week">Week</button>
  <button role="tab" aria-selected="false" tabindex="-1" data-v="month">Month</button>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl } from './segmented-control/SegmentedControl';

const options = [
  { value: 'day', label: 'Day' },
  { value: 'week', label: 'Week' },
  { value: 'month', label: 'Month' },
];

const [range, setRange] = useState('day');

<SegmentedControl label="Range" options={options} value={range} onValueChange={setRange} />
<SegmentedControl label="Density" as="radio" options={options} defaultValue="week" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [SegmentedControlComponent] -->
<dm-segmented-control label="Range" [options]="options"
  [value]="range" (valueChange)="range = $event" />
<dm-segmented-control label="Density" as="radio" [options]="options" defaultValue="week" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/segmented_control.dart';

SegmentedControl(
  label: 'Range',
  options: const [
    SegmentOption('day', label: 'Day'),
    SegmentOption('week', label: 'Week'),
    SegmentOption('month', label: 'Month'),
  ],
  value: range,
  onValueChange: (v) => setState(() => range = v),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{ value: string; label: ReactNode }[]` | The choices, in order, left to right. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string` | The picked value. Pass `value` with `onValueChange` for a controlled control. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | Fires with the new value when the pick changes. |
| `label` | `string` | Names the group for screen readers, like `View`. Required. |
| `as` | `tabs \| radio` | `tabs` (the default) when it switches a panel, `radio` when it sets an option. |
| `id` | `string` | Ties the tabs to their panel: give the panel an id of the form "id-panel" and point its aria-labelledby at "id-value". Defaults to a generated id. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
track and sliding knob take the active theme's surface and accent colors; in Blueprint the control
is squared off, in Soft it is a pill with a rounder knob.


# Stat cards (/docs/components/stat-cards)

Stat cards are a row of numbers that matter. Each card has an icon, a label, the value in large
type, its change against the period before (green from zero, red below), and a sparkline in its own
colour. A `period` switch along the top rolls the numbers to their new values and redraws every
line.

<Preview>
  <StatCardsExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + stat-cards.css -->
<div class="dm-scx">
  <div class="dm-scx-grid">
    <div class="dm-scx-c dm-panel">
      <span class="dm-scx-k">Agent runs</span>
      <div class="dm-scx-v">
        <b class="dm-num">1,842</b>
        <span class="dm-scx-d dm-tag dm-ok dm-up">+12.4%</span>
      </div>
      <div class="dm-scx-sp">
        <svg viewBox="0 0 100 30" preserveAspectRatio="none">
          <path d="M0 24 L100 4" />
        </svg>
      </div>
    </div>
    <!-- one .dm-scx-c per stat -->
  </div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { StatCards } from './stat-cards/StatCards';

const stats = [
  {
    icon: 'spark',
    label: 'Agent runs',
    values: [
      { value: 1842, change: 12.4, points: [980, 1120, 1070, 1260, 1410, 1550, 1842] },
      { value: 7320, change: 8.1, points: [5200, 5600, 5900, 6100, 6600, 6950, 7320] },
    ],
  },
  { icon: 'coins', label: 'Cost', prefix: '$', values: [/* one entry per period */] },
];

const periods = [
  { label: '7 days', compare: 'vs previous 7 days' },
  { label: '30 days', compare: 'vs previous 30 days' },
];

<StatCards stats={stats} periods={periods} defaultPeriod={0} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [StatCardsComponent] -->
<dm-stat-cards
  [stats]="stats"
  [periods]="periods"
  [defaultPeriod]="0"
  (periodChange)="onPeriod($event)"
></dm-stat-cards>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/stat_cards.dart';

StatCards(
  stats: [
    StatCardsStat(
      icon: IconName.spark,
      label: 'Agent runs',
      values: [
        StatCardsValue(value: 1842, change: 12.4, points: [980, 1120, 1260, 1410, 1842]),
        StatCardsValue(value: 7320, change: 8.1, points: [5200, 5900, 6600, 6950, 7320]),
      ],
    ),
  ],
  periods: const [
    StatCardsPeriod(label: '7 days', compare: 'vs previous 7 days'),
    StatCardsPeriod(label: '30 days', compare: 'vs previous 30 days'),
  ],
  defaultPeriod: 0,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stats` | `StatCardsStat[]` | The cards. Each has an `icon`, `label`, one `values` entry per period, and optional `prefix`, `suffix` and `color`. |
| `periods` | `StatCardsPeriod[]` | The switch options. Each has a `label` and an optional `compare` line shown on hover. |
| `period` | `number` | The period on show, by index. Leave it out to let the switch pick it. |
| `defaultPeriod` | `number` | The period shown first when uncontrolled. Defaults to `0`. |
| `onPeriodChange` | `(period: number) => void` | Called with the new index when the switch changes. |
| `sparkRange` | `[number, number]` | The bottom and top of every sparkline. Defaults to each card's own range. |

Each `StatCardsStat` carries `values: { value, change, points }[]` — one entry per period, in the
same order as `periods` — where `value` is the number, `change` is the percent against the period
before, and `points` is the sparkline oldest first.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the cards are squared off with hairline borders; in Soft they are rounded panels with a
softer shadow. The sparkline colours fall back to the chart palette (the accent, then violet, green
and orange) unless a card sets its own `color`.


# Status pill (/docs/components/status-pill)

A status pill shows a single line of what the agent is up to. Its `state` picks the glyph and
colour — `thinking`, `reading` and `working` shimmer while they run — and a new `state`, `label`,
`file` or `action` fades the old line out before the new one arrives. The `bar` variant is taller
and draws a `progress` track along its bottom.

<Preview>
  <StatusPillExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + status-pill.css -->
<div class="dm-spl">
  <div class="dm-spl-pill" aria-live="polite">
    <div class="dm-spl-in">
      <span class="dm-g"><!-- glyph --></span>
      <span class="dm-shim">Reading repository</span>
      <span class="dm-m">2 of 4</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- bar variant with a progress track -->
<div class="dm-spl dm-bar">
  <div class="dm-spl-pill" aria-live="polite">
    <div class="dm-spl-in">
      <span class="dm-g"><!-- glyph --></span>
      <span class="dm-shim">Writing tests</span>
    </div>
    <div class="dm-spl-track"><div class="dm-spl-fill" style="width:80%"></div></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { StatusPill } from './status-pill/StatusPill';

<StatusPill state="reading" label="Reading repository" meta="2 of 4" />
<StatusPill state="working" label="Editing" file={{ name: 'PricingCard.tsx', type: 'tsx' }} />
<StatusPill state="waiting" label="Needs your review" action={{ label: 'Open', onClick: open }} />
<StatusPill variant="bar" state="working" label="Writing tests" progress={80} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [StatusPillComponent] -->
<dm-status-pill state="reading" label="Reading repository" meta="2 of 4" />
<dm-status-pill state="working" label="Editing" [file]="{ name: 'PricingCard.tsx', type: 'tsx' }" />
<dm-status-pill state="waiting" label="Needs your review" [action]="{ label: 'Open', onClick: open }" />
<dm-status-pill variant="bar" state="working" label="Writing tests" [progress]="80" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/status_pill.dart';

const StatusPill(state: StatusPillState.reading, label: 'Reading repository', meta: '2 of 4'),
const StatusPill(state: StatusPillState.working, label: 'Editing', file: StatusFile('PricingCard.tsx', type: 'tsx')),
StatusPill(state: StatusPillState.waiting, label: 'Needs your review', action: StatusAction('Open', onClick: open)),
const StatusPill(variant: StatusPillVariant.bar, state: StatusPillState.working, label: 'Writing tests', progress: 80),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | What the agent is doing, in a few words. Required. |
| `state` | `idle \| thinking \| reading \| working \| waiting \| done` | Picks the glyph and colour. `thinking`, `reading` and `working` shimmer while they run. |
| `meta` | `string` | Quiet detail after the label, like "2 of 4". Changing only this does not restart the pill. |
| `file` | `{ name: string; type?: string }` | A file chip after the label. |
| `action` | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` | A button at the end, for when the agent needs the person. |
| `progress` | `number` | 0 to 100, drawn as a track along the bottom of the `bar` variant. |
| `variant` | `pill \| bar` | `pill` hugs its content; `bar` is taller and leaves room for the progress track. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The pill
sits on a surface with the shared shadow, so it picks up the theme's surface and token colours; in
Soft it is rounder, and in dark it reads against the dark stage.


# Step Loader (/docs/components/step-loader)

A step loader shows an agent's work as named steps. The step running now sits beside a small
loader; a track below fills as steps finish; and the row expands to the full list, each line
switching to its `done` text once complete. When `current` reaches the number of steps, every step
is done and the row shows the `doneLabel`.

<Preview>
  <StepLoaderExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + step-loader.css -->
<div class="stl dm">
  <button class="stl-row" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="stl-g"></span>
    <span class="stl-t"><span class="stl-lab shim">Reading Figma frames</span></span>
    <span class="stl-n num">1/4</span>
    <svg class="i xs stl-chev"><use href="#i-chev-d" /></svg>
  </button>
  <div class="stl-track"><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i></div>
  <div class="fold shut stl-fold"><div><ol class="stl-list"></ol></div></div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { StepLoader } from './step-loader/StepLoader';

const steps = [
  { label: 'Reading Figma frames', done: 'Read 4 frames' },
  { label: 'Generating components', done: 'Made 6 components' },
  { label: 'Writing tests' },
];

<StepLoader steps={steps} current={1} loader="radar" />
<StepLoader steps={steps} current={steps.length} doneLabel="Ready for review" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [StepLoaderComponent] -->
<dm-step-loader [steps]="steps" [current]="1" loader="radar" />
<dm-step-loader [steps]="steps" [current]="steps.length" doneLabel="Ready for review" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/step_loader.dart';

StepLoader(
  steps: const [
    Step('Reading Figma frames', done: 'Read 4 frames'),
    Step('Generating components', done: 'Made 6 components'),
    Step('Writing tests'),
  ],
  current: 1,
  loader: StepLoaderGlyph.radar,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `{ label: string; done?: string }[]` | The steps. `label` shows while running, `done` once finished (falls back to `label`). |
| `current` | `number` | Index of the step running now. `steps.length` or more means every step is done. |
| `loader` | `radar \| dots \| ring \| bars` | The loader glyph beside the running step. `radar` by default. |
| `doneLabel` | `string` | Label once every step is done. `Ready for review` by default. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | Whether the full list is open. Leave `open` out to let the row toggle it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `callback` | Fires when the row opens or closes the list. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
track and loader take the accent color from the active theme; in Soft the row and track are softer
and more rounded than in Blueprint.


# Thinking States (/docs/components/thinking-states)

A thinking state is a small animated mark beside a status line. Pick one of six marks with
`variant`; give it `steps` and, with more than one, they take turns every `interval` unless you
drive the index with `current`. An elapsed-seconds counter sits at the end of the line and counts
by itself unless you set `seconds` or hide it with `seconds={false}`.

<Preview>
  <ThinkingStatesExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + thinking-states.css -->
<div class="ths" data-v="orbit">
  <div class="ths-row">
    <span class="ths-mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="ths-l" aria-hidden="true">
      <span class="ths-tx shim">Thinking</span>
      <span class="ths-car" hidden></span>
    </span>
    <span class="ths-t num" aria-hidden="true">0s</span>
  </div>
  <span class="ths-sr" role="status" aria-live="polite">Thinking</span>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ThinkingStates } from './thinking-states/ThinkingStates';

const steps = ['Thinking', 'Reading 3 files', 'Planning the change'];

<ThinkingStates variant="orbit" steps={steps} />
<ThinkingStates variant="stream" steps={steps} interval={2600} />
<ThinkingStates variant="scan" steps={steps} seconds={false} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ThinkingStatesComponent] -->
<dm-thinking-states variant="orbit" [steps]="steps" />
<dm-thinking-states variant="stream" [steps]="steps" [interval]="2600" />
<dm-thinking-states variant="scan" [steps]="steps" [seconds]="false" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/thinking_states.dart';

const steps = ['Thinking', 'Reading 3 files', 'Planning the change'];

ThinkingStates(variant: ThinkingVariant.orbit, steps: steps),
ThinkingStates(variant: ThinkingVariant.stream, steps: steps, interval: 2600),
ThinkingStates(variant: ThinkingVariant.scan, steps: steps, seconds: false),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `orbit \| morph \| scan \| stream \| matrix \| stack` | Which indicator to draw. `orbit` by default. |
| `steps` | `string[]` | The status lines. With more than one they take turns unless `current` is set. |
| `current` | `number` | Index of the line to show. Leave it out to let the lines take turns by themselves. |
| `interval` | `number` | Milliseconds each line shows for when they take turns. `2600` by default. |
| `seconds` | `number \| false` | Seconds shown at the end of the line. Counts by itself when left out; `false` hides it. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
marks and the typed line use the active theme's accent and text colors; the counter is set in the
numeric style. Motion is paused for readers who prefer reduced motion — the line is shown whole
rather than typed.


# Thinking (/docs/components/thinking)

A thinking trace is the reasoning log an agent writes as it works. Each step arrives on a line that
spins while it runs and turns into a green check once it finishes, with what it found written under
it and how long it took at its right. The header counts seconds while it runs; once the last step
lands it becomes a summary of the work and the trace folds itself away.

<Preview>
  <ThinkingExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + thinking.css -->
<div class="tk" data-open="1">
  <button class="tk-h" aria-expanded="true">
    <span class="tk-mark"><span class="think on"><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i></span></span>
    <span class="tk-title shim">Checking the pricing page</span>
    <span class="tk-time num">0s</span>
    <svg class="i xs tk-chev"><use href="#i-chev-d"/></svg>
  </button>
  <div class="fold tk-fold"><div><ol class="tk-list" aria-live="polite"></ol></div></div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Thinking } from './thinking/Thinking';

<Thinking
  running={running}
  title="Checking the pricing page"
  summary="3 cards to fix, 2 changes planned"
  steps={[
    { label: 'Measure the plan cards', state: 'done', result: '3 cards are off the 8px grid', time: '1.4s' },
    { label: 'Plan the fix', state: 'running' },
  ]}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ThinkingComponent] -->
<dm-thinking
  [running]="running"
  title="Checking the pricing page"
  summary="3 cards to fix, 2 changes planned"
  [steps]="steps"
></dm-thinking>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/thinking.dart';

Thinking(
  running: running,
  title: 'Checking the pricing page',
  summary: '3 cards to fix, 2 changes planned',
  steps: const [
    ThinkingStep(label: 'Measure the plan cards', state: ThinkingStepState.done, result: '3 cards are off the 8px grid', time: '1.4s'),
    ThinkingStep(label: 'Plan the fix', state: ThinkingStepState.running),
  ],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `ThinkingStep[]` | The steps the agent has taken so far. Each has a `label`, a `state` of `running`, `retry` or `done`, an optional `result` and `time`. |
| `running` | `boolean` | Spins, counts seconds and keeps the trace open while true. |
| `seconds` | `number` | Seconds to show. Leave it out to let it count while running. |
| `title` | `string` | The header while it runs, like "Checking the pricing page". |
| `summary` | `string` | The header once it is done. Defaults to the number of steps. |
| `collapseWhenDone` | `boolean` | Folds the trace away a moment after it finishes. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | Whether the trace is open. Leave `open` out to let the header toggle it. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
running step turns in the accent with a soft halo, finished steps and the rail between them turn
green, and a slow step waits in amber. In Blueprint the marks are squared off and the result writes
in with a plain fade instead of a blur.


# Toast (/docs/components/toast)

A toast is a short message on a surface. Its `tone` picks the icon and colour — `loading` spins —
and it takes a `title`, an optional `description` and an optional `action` button. Pass a new `id`
to slide a new toast in and the old one away; keep the same `id` to change the text in place.

<Preview>
  <ToastExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + toast.css -->
<div class="dm-tst-slot" aria-live="polite">
  <div class="dm-tst-t dm-tst-in" role="status">
    <span class="dm-g"><!-- tone icon --></span>
    <div class="dm-tx"><b>Deploy succeeded</b><span>Live in production.</span></div>
    <div class="dm-acts">
      <button class="dm-pill dm-sm dm-ghost">Undo</button>
      <button class="dm-ib" aria-label="Dismiss"><!-- x --></button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Toast, type ToastData } from './toast/Toast';

const [toast, setToast] = useState<ToastData | null>(null);

setToast({ id: 1, tone: 'success', title: 'Deploy succeeded', description: 'Live in production.' });
setToast({
  id: 2,
  tone: 'error',
  title: 'Build failed',
  action: { label: 'Retry', onClick: retry, variant: 'primary' },
});

<Toast toast={toast} onDismiss={() => setToast(null)} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ToastComponent] -->
toast: ToastData | null = {
  id: 1, tone: 'success', title: 'Deploy succeeded', description: 'Live in production.'
};

<dm-toast [toast]="toast" (dismiss)="toast = null" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/toast.dart';

ToastData? toast = const ToastData(
  id: 1, tone: ToastTone.success, title: 'Deploy succeeded', description: 'Live in production.',
);

Toast(toast: toast, onDismiss: (id) => setState(() => toast = null)),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toast` | `ToastData \| null` | The toast to show, or `null` for none. |
| `onDismiss` | `(id) => void` | Called by the close button. The toast leaves either way. |
| `toast.id` | `string \| number` | A new id slides a new toast in and the old one away. Keep it to change text in place. |
| `toast.tone` | `success \| error \| info \| loading` | Picks the icon and its colour. `loading` spins. |
| `toast.title` | `string` | The bold first line. |
| `toast.description` | `string` | The quieter line under the title. Crossfades when it changes. |
| `toast.action` | `{ label; onClick; variant?: ghost \| primary \| ink; busy? }` | A button before the close button, like Undo or Retry. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a surface with the toast shadow and its tone tints come from the theme tokens, so it reads
against the dark stage; in Soft the card and its buttons are rounder.


# Tooltip (/docs/components/tooltip)

A tooltip is the label that waits a moment under a toolbar button, then follows the pointer
instantly as it moves between them. Buttons come in `groups` with a line between, each with a `tip`
and an optional shortcut (`kbd`). Avatars at the end get a richer card instead — a person's name,
role and what they are doing now, with an agent shown by its thinking dots.

<Preview>
  <TooltipExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + tooltip.css -->
<div class="dm-ttp">
  <div class="dm-ttp-bar dm-panel">
    <button class="dm-ib" aria-label="Undo" data-tip="Undo" data-kbd="⌘Z">↶</button>
    <button class="dm-ib" aria-label="Redo" data-tip="Redo" data-kbd="⌘⇧Z">↷</button>
    <span class="dm-ttp-sep"></span>
    <button class="dm-ib" aria-label="Ask agent" data-tip="Ask the agent" data-kbd="⌘J">✦</button>
    <span class="dm-ttp-sep"></span>
    <span class="dm-ttp-avs">
      <button class="dm-ttp-av" aria-label="Mira Chen">MC</button>
    </span>
  </div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from './tooltip/Tooltip';

const groups = [
  [
    { key: 'undo', icon: 'undo', label: 'Undo', kbd: '⌘Z' },
    { key: 'ask', icon: 'spark', label: 'Ask agent', tip: 'Ask the agent', kbd: '⌘J' },
  ],
  [{ key: 'share', icon: 'users', label: 'Share', tip: 'Share with your team' }],
];

const people = [
  { key: 'mira', initials: 'MC', color: 'var(--dm-av-l)', name: 'Mira Chen', role: 'Design lead', status: 'Editing Pricing, frame 2' },
  { key: 'agent', initials: 'AI', color: 'var(--dm-av-p)', name: 'Visuno agent', role: 'Assistant', status: 'Drafting release notes', working: true },
];

<Tooltip groups={groups} people={people} note="Hover a button for its tip." />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [TooltipComponent] -->
<dm-tooltip
  [groups]="groups"
  [people]="people"
  note="Hover a button for its tip."
></dm-tooltip>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/tooltip.dart';

Tooltip(
  groups: [
    [
      TooltipTool(key: 'undo', icon: IconName.undo, label: 'Undo', kbd: '⌘Z'),
      TooltipTool(key: 'ask', icon: IconName.spark, label: 'Ask agent', tip: 'Ask the agent', kbd: '⌘J'),
    ],
    [TooltipTool(key: 'share', icon: IconName.users, label: 'Share', tip: 'Share with your team')],
  ],
  people: const [
    TooltipPerson(key: 'mira', initials: 'MC', color: 'var(--dm-av-l)', name: 'Mira Chen', role: 'Design lead', status: 'Editing Pricing, frame 2'),
    TooltipPerson(key: 'agent', initials: 'AI', color: 'var(--dm-av-p)', name: 'Visuno agent', role: 'Assistant', status: 'Drafting release notes', working: true),
  ],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `groups` | `TooltipTool[][]` | The toolbar's buttons, in groups with a line between. Each tool is `{ key, icon, label, tip?, kbd?, onClick? }`. |
| `people` | `TooltipPerson[]` | Avatars at the end. Each is `{ key, initials, color, name, role, status, working? }`; hovering one shows a card. |
| `note` | `ReactNode` | A quiet line under the toolbar. |
| `cardDelay` | `number` | How long a person card waits before it shows. Defaults to `300`. |
| `openTip` | `string \| null` | Shows this tool's tip by key, as if hovered. Leave it out to let the pointer decide. |
| `openCard` | `string \| null` | Shows this person's card by key, as if hovered. |

A tool's `tip` overrides its `label` in the tooltip, so set it only when the tip should say more
than the button's name; the `kbd` shortcut is shown after it. A person's `working: true` swaps the
green status dot for the agent's thinking dots.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the bar and card are squared off with hairline borders; in Soft they are rounded panels.
The tooltip itself and the avatar colours (`--dm-av-*`) come from the theme, so they stay legible on
either background.


# Trace view (/docs/components/trace-view)

A trace view lays one agent run out as a waterfall. Every span — an LLM call, a tool call, a
retrieval, a sub-agent — sits on a shared time axis, nested under the span that started it with a
tree's guides. Each kind has its own colour, counted in the key. While the run streams, a playhead
marks now and running bars glow at their leading edge; a tool call that runs over its budget turns
amber and hatched and is tagged slow. Open any span to see where it sat in the run, its input, its
output, its latency and its tokens.

<Preview>
  <TraceViewExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + trace-view.css, then the component script -->
<div class="card wide" data-c="trace-view">
  <div class="stage-in">
    <div class="trv panel">
      <div class="trv-h">
        <div class="trv-ht"><b>Pricing research</b><span class="muted trv-st" aria-live="polite"></span></div>
        <span class="trv-tot num">0.00s</span>
      </div>
      <div class="trv-lg" role="list" aria-label="Spans by kind"></div>
      <div class="trv-ax" aria-hidden="true"><span>Span</span><span class="trv-sc"></span><span class="trv-tk">Tokens</span><span class="trv-ms">Time</span></div>
      <div class="trv-rows" role="group" aria-label="Spans"></div>
      <div class="fold shut trv-dt" inert><div><div class="trv-dc" role="region" aria-label="Span details"></div></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { TraceView } from './trace-view/TraceView';

const spans = [
  { id: 'run', name: 'Pricing research', kind: 'agent', start: 0, duration: 4.82, children: [
    { id: 'plan', name: 'Plan the steps', kind: 'llm', start: 0.04, duration: 0.62, tokens: 1240 },
    { id: 'fetch', name: 'fetch_page', kind: 'tool', start: 1.12, duration: 2.46, tokens: 3120 },
  ] },
];

<TraceView title="Pricing research" spans={spans} axis={5} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [TraceViewComponent] -->
spans: TraceSpan[] = [
  { id: 'run', name: 'Pricing research', kind: 'agent', start: 0, duration: 4.82, children: [
    { id: 'plan', name: 'Plan the steps', kind: 'llm', start: 0.04, duration: 0.62, tokens: 1240 },
    { id: 'fetch', name: 'fetch_page', kind: 'tool', start: 1.12, duration: 2.46, tokens: 3120 },
  ] },
];
```

```html
<dm-trace-view
  title="Pricing research"
  [spans]="spans"
  [axis]="5"
  (selectedChange)="onSelect($event)"
></dm-trace-view>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/trace_view.dart';

TraceView(
  title: 'Pricing research',
  axis: 5,
  spans: const [
    TraceSpan(id: 'run', name: 'Pricing research', kind: SpanKind.agent, start: 0, duration: 4.82, children: [
      TraceSpan(id: 'plan', name: 'Plan the steps', kind: SpanKind.llm, start: 0.04, duration: 0.62, tokens: 1240),
      TraceSpan(id: 'fetch', name: 'fetch_page', kind: SpanKind.tool, start: 1.12, duration: 2.46, tokens: 3120),
    ]),
  ],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The run's name, shown over the status line. |
| `spans` | `TraceSpan[]` | The run's top spans, usually one root with everything nested under it. |
| `time` | `number` | Seconds into the run while it streams in. Spans that start later stay hidden, running ones reach this far. Leave it out once the run is over. |
| `axis` | `number` | Seconds the time axis covers. Defaults to the run's length, rounded up to a whole second. |
| `slowAfter` | `number` | A tool call longer than this many seconds turns amber and is tagged slow. Defaults to 2. |
| `status` | `string` | Overrides the status line. Defaults to "Running · 4 spans", then "Done · 7 spans, 1 slow". |
| `selected` | `string` | The id of the open span, whose details show under the waterfall. null closes them. |
| `onSelectedChange` / `selectedChange` | `callback` | Fires with the id of the span opened, or null when the details close. |

A `TraceSpan` has an `id`, a `name`, a `kind` (agent, llm, tool, or retrieval), a `start` and
`duration` in seconds, optional `tokens`, optional `input` and `output` strings, and optional
`children`. An agent span without its own token count adds up every span under it.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the bars square off and running bars switch from a sweeping sheen to a steady stripe. Each
kind keeps its colour from the chart palette; a slow bar is amber and hatched in every theme.


# Web search (/docs/components/web-search)

Web search shows an agent researching out loud. Each query is a row with how many results came
back and how long it took; a query that finds nothing is asked again in other words. Under each
query sit the pages it opened, each marked Read, Skimmed, or Skipped with the reason (paywall,
blocked, timeout). Once the run is done the trail folds to one line and the answer streams in,
its bracketed numbers pointing back at the pages that back them up.

<Preview>
  <WebSearchExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['Vanilla', 'React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="Vanilla">

```html
<!-- include core.css + web-search.css, then the component script -->
<div class="card bare" data-c="web-search">
  <div class="stage-in">
    <div class="wsx panel">
      <button class="wsx-h" aria-expanded="true">
        <span class="wsx-ic"><span class="spin"></span></span>
        <span class="wsx-st shim">Searching the web</span>
        <span class="wsx-marks" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      </button>
      <div class="fold wsx-fold"><div><div class="wsx-list"></div></div></div>
      <div class="wsx-ans"></div>
      <p class="wsx-sr" role="status"></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { WebSearch } from './web-search/WebSearch';

const queries = [
  { key: 'q1', query: 'stripe usage-based billing limits', status: 'done', results: 5, time: '0.9s',
    pages: [
      { title: 'Meters and billing thresholds', domain: 'stripe.com', date: 'Sep 2026', status: 'read', cite: 1 },
      { title: 'Why SaaS pricing is moving to usage', domain: 'ft.com', status: 'paywall' },
    ] },
];

<WebSearch
  queries={queries}
  done
  answer="Stripe caps metered usage at 100 million events a month [1]."
  bare={false}
/>
```

</Tab>

```html
    pages: [
      { title: 'Meters and billing thresholds', domain: 'stripe.com', date: 'Sep 2026', status: 'read', cite: 1 },
      { title: 'Why SaaS pricing is moving to usage', domain: 'ft.com', status: 'paywall' },
    ] },
];
```

```html
<dm-web-search
  [queries]="queries"
  [done]="true"
  answer="Stripe caps metered usage at 100 million events a month [1]."
  [bare]="false"
  (openChange)="onOpen($event)"
></dm-web-search>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/web_search.dart';

WebSearch(
  queries: const [
    WebQuery(
      key: 'q1',
      query: 'stripe usage-based billing limits',
      results: 5,
      time: '0.9s',
      pages: [
        WebPage(title: 'Meters and billing thresholds', domain: 'stripe.com', date: 'Sep 2026', status: WebPageStatus.read, cite: 1),
        WebPage(title: 'Why SaaS pricing is moving to usage', domain: 'ft.com', status: WebPageStatus.paywall),
      ],
    ),
  ],
  done: true,
  answer: 'Stripe caps metered usage at 100 million events a month [1].',
  bare: false,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queries` | `WebQuery[]` | The searches, in order. Each has a key, the query text, a status, a result count, a time, an optional rewritten flag, and its pages. |
| `done` | `boolean` | True once searching and reading are over. The trail folds to its summary line. |
| `answer` | `string` | The answer, with sources cited as numbers in brackets. Each number points at the page with that cite value. |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the trail is open. Left out, it folds once `done` turns true. |
| `onOpenChange` / `openChange` | `callback` | Fires when the trail is opened or closed. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Without the panel, for a chat stream. True by default. |

A `WebPage` has a `title`, a `domain`, an optional `date`, a `status` (reading, read, skimmed,
paywall, blocked, or timeout), and an optional `cite` number the answer refers to it by.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). Skipped
pages dim and their tag turns amber; a running page shows a spinner. The site initials stack on the
header, and hovering a citation lights the page that backs it up along with its site mark.


# Introduction (/docs)

**Visuno** is an open-source UI component library for building agent interfaces. Every component
ships natively for **Vanilla JS**, **React**, **Angular**, and **Flutter**, built from a single
shared set of design tokens — so a component looks and behaves the same wherever you use it.

Each component in these docs has a **live preview** you can toggle between light/dark and the two
styles, plus the code for all four frameworks side by side.

## Four frameworks, one design [#four-frameworks-one-design]

| Framework | Form |
|-----------|------|
| **Vanilla JS** | Plain HTML + CSS + JS — no build step, drop it in |
| **React** | `.tsx` components (requires React 19) |
| **Angular** | Standalone components (`dm-*` selectors, Angular 17+) |
| **Flutter** | Dart widgets, themed to match the web |

The Vanilla and React versions are the reference; Angular and Flutter are native ports that mirror
the same props and behavior.

## Theming [#theming]

Every component responds to the same two switches, so your whole UI changes at once:

- **Dark mode** — `data-theme="dark"` on a parent element (web); `Brightness.dark` in the Flutter
  theme.
- **Style** — the default **Blueprint** style, or **Soft** via `data-style="soft"` (web). Blueprint
  is crisp and squared; Soft is rounded and plush.

Design tokens (`--dm-*` on the web, `DmColors`/`DmSpace`/`DmRadius` in Flutter) drive every color,
space, radius, and motion — change a token once and it flows everywhere.

## Sections [#sections]

Components are grouped by what they do in an agent product:

- **Agent status** — show what the agent is doing: live status, thinking states, reasoning trails,
  action logs, run timelines, cost and context meters.
- **Charts and tables** — present data: stat cards and more.
- **Dates** — pick and switch: segmented controls and date tools.
- **Forms and inputs** — the basics: buttons, badges, progress, tooltips.

## Get started [#get-started]

<Cards>
  <Card title="Browse components" href="/docs/components/status-pill" description="Live previews and code for every component." />
  <Card title="Components on GitHub" href="https://github.com/Visuno/components" description="The source for all four frameworks." />
</Cards>

Pick a component from the sidebar, copy the snippet for your framework, and drop it in. Pull the
shared core once (tokens + helpers), and every component you add just works.
